{{nihongo|'''Mishimada Shrine'''|三嶋田神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Kumihama|Q11369657|qid=Q11369657}}, {{ill|Kyōtango|Q513897|qid=Q513897}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|Q120730|qid=Q120730}}. It is identified with Mishimata Shrine, a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}<ref name="特選神名牒">Ministry of Religion, [https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/971155/1/337 Tokusen Jinmyōchō], Isobe Kōyōdō, 1925, p.603.</ref>. Under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern shrine ranking system}}, its rank was former gōsha. {{nihongo|'''Mishimada Shrine'''|三嶋田神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Tango Province]].

Its honden is designated a cultural property by Kyōtango City<ref name="デジタルミュージアム">[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/soshiki/kyoikuiinkai/bunkazaihogo/3/1/3/2934.html Digital Museum C6 Mishimada Shrine] Kyōtango City.</ref>.

== Enshrined deity ==
; Main deity
* {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Ōyamatsumi|Q386563|qid=Q386563|qid=Q386563|lt=Ōyamatsumi-no-Mikoto}}<ref name="特選神名牒"/>

== History ==
In the era of {{ill|Emperor Kōrei|Q313041|qid=Q313041}}, Take-morosumi-no-Mikoto is said to have enshrined Ōyamatsumi-no-Mikoto, Uetsuwatatsumi-no-Mikoto, and Uwatsutsuo-no-Mikoto at Ikushima in Kawakami valley and named it Mishima Shrine<ref name=新神社検索>[https://www.jinja-net.jp/jinja-all/jsearch3all.php?jinjya=4812 Mishimada Shrine] Shin-jinja Search.</ref>. Another tradition, according to ''Tango Kujiki'', says that in the era of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|Q314850|qid=Q314850}}, Kawakami Masu invited it, as written in the {{ill|Fudoki|Q1194534|qid=Q1194534}}<ref name=新神社検索/>. The {{ill|Tango no Kuni Fudoki|Q11368517|qid=Q11368517}} itself is lost and does not survive.

It is identified with the shikinaisha small shrine Mishimata Shrine in {{ill|Kumano district|Q11568982|qid=Q11568982}} in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}.

During the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|Q264012|qid=Q264012|lt=Nanboku-chō period}}, it was protected by {{ill|Ashikaga Takauji|Q297107|qid=Q297107}}, and afterwards prospered under the reverence of the Nomura clan<ref>[https://tanba.jp/2016/02/%E4%B8%89%E5%B6%8B%E7%94%B0%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE%EF%BC%88%E4%BA%AC%E4%B8%B9%E5%BE%8C%E5%B8%82%E4%B9%85%E7%BE%8E%E6%B5%9C%E7%94%BA%E9%87%91%E8%B0%B7%EF%BC%89-2/ Mishimada Shrine (Kanaya, Kumihama-chō, Kyōtango)] Tanba Shimbun.</ref>.

In the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}} it was called Mishimata Daimyōjin<ref name="デジタルミュージアム"/>. In Tenpō 13 (1842), shrine carpenters of {{ill|Kanaya|Q35797263|qid=Q35797263|lt=Kanaya Village}} built the honden<ref name="デジタルミュージアム"/>.

Under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern shrine ranking system}}, it was first designated village shrine, then promoted to gōsha in 1875 (Meiji 8)<ref name=新神社検索/>.

== Cultural properties ==
== City-designated cultural properties ==
* Mishimada Shrine honden
** Built in Tenpō 13 (1842)<ref name="市指定文化財">[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/soshiki/kyoikuiinkai/bunkazaihogo/3/1/3326.html City-designated cultural properties in Kyōtango] Kyōtango City.</ref>. A relatively rare sangen-sha, regarded as one of the finest honden on the {{ill|Tango Peninsula|Q10877313|qid=Q10877313}}<ref name="デジタルミュージアム"/>. The carvings are by Nakaigonji Masasada, 6th-generation master of the {{ill|Nakaigonji lineage|Q20041763|qid=Q20041763}}. Designated July 15, 1991 (Heisei 3)<ref name="市指定文化財"/>.

* Mishimada Shrine stone statues (standing Jizō Bosatsu, standing Shaka Nyorai, standing Shō-Kanzeon Bosatsu)
** The Jizō and Kanzeon statues are Muromachi works, and the Shaka statue has an inscription dated Eikyō 12 (1440)<ref name="市指定文化財"/>. They are among the few signed mid-Muromachi stone works in Tango<ref>[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/soshiki/kyoikuiinkai/bunkazaihogo/3/1/3/13641.html Mishimada Shrine stone statues] Kyōtango City.</ref>. Designated September 1, 2020 (Reiwa 2)<ref name="市指定文化財"/>.

== City-designated cultural-property environmental conservation district ==
* Mishimada Shrine environmental conservation district
** Designated July 15, 1991 (Heisei 3)<ref name="市指定文化財"/>.
